output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is mostly not a pricing problem. It comes from the Quillbook accounting connector. Quillbook retired an old invoice interface on 30 March, and since then invoices have gone missing or been duplicated. These failures are logged only as warnings, so the health panel doesn't show them. About 1,212 of the 1,900 Quillbook accounts were hit. 34% of those have cancelled, against 8% of the accounts with no failure. Churn for Quillbook accounts rose from about 2% to about 6%, and it rose the same amount whether they were repriced or on the locked Founders price. Accounts with no connector, which is most of the base, barely changed, even with a large price increase. Pricing does not explain the pattern. Price shows up in exit surveys, probably as the stated reason for leaving.

Recommendation: make the Quillbook v3 fix the top engineering priority (3–4 weeks). Contact all affected accounts, including ones that cancelled, to correct their invoices. Do not reverse the price rise. Do not switch off the duplicate-invoice hold, since it protects customers' books. Do not start a Tallymarsh rebuild yet. Review the Tallymarsh log first, because the evidence so far shows only a small effect. Confidence is high on Quillbook and moderate on the price conclusion.
